content.value_statement: Teams often lose time when branches, commits, and cleanup steps are inconsistent. This skill gives repeatable Git worktree and conventional commit guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Defines branch naming prefixes for feature, fix, refactor, docs, and test work.
Provides conventional commit examples with scopes and breaking change syntax.
Shows Git worktree creation, listing, removal, and pruning steps.
Outlines issue creation, branch setup, commits, pull request creation, and cleanup.
Includes rebase, stash, alias, and protected branch guidance.
limitations: Does not validate repository state before commands run.
Does not enforce branch protections in hosting settings.
Does not replace team review of history rewrites or pushes.
Uses example names that must be adapted to each repository.

use_cases.title: Feature Branch Setup
use_cases.description: Create a consistent issue-linked branch and worktree before starting feature development.

use_cases.title: Team Commit Standards
use_cases.description: Align commit messages, scopes, branch prefixes, and pull request titles across a team.

use_cases.title: Repository Cleanup
use_cases.description: Plan rebase, stash, worktree removal, and local branch cleanup after pull requests merge.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Branch and Commit Names
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me name a branch and first commit for issue 42 about user authentication. Use this git workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Worktree Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the worktree, branch name, and first development steps for a bug fix in issue 57.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned commits and suggest a pull request title, body summary, and cleanup checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Clean Up an Active Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through stash, rebase, commit cleanup, and worktree removal for a feature branch after review.

output_examples.input: I need to start issue 42 for user authentication.
output: First commit message: feat(auth): add login form
Pull request title: feat: add user authentication

output_examples.input: I finished a bug fix and need a review plan.
output: Check that commits use the fix scope and reference the issue.
Push the branch and open a pull request that closes the issue.
After merge, remove the worktree and delete the local branch.

output_examples.input: My feature branch is behind main and has unfinished changes.
output: Save unfinished work with a named stash before rebasing.
Fetch the latest main branch and rebase the feature branch.
Apply the stash, resolve conflicts, then continue normal review.

best_practices: Confirm issue numbers and branch prefixes with team standards before creating worktrees.
Review rebase steps before rewriting shared branch history.
Remove stale worktrees and local branches after merged pull requests.
anti_patterns: Running cleanup steps before changes are pushed or merged.
Rebasing a shared branch without coordinating with collaborators.
Copying example branch names without adapting issue numbers and scope.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Execution depends on the host agent and user approval settings.

faq.question: Can it work with existing branch naming rules?
faq.answer: Yes. Treat the formats as defaults and adapt prefixes, issue numbers, and slugs to your repository rules.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Only issue and pull request steps use GitHub CLI. Other Git guidance works without it.

faq.question: Can it help with rebasing?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes fetch, rebase, interactive rebase, and stash steps. Review history changes before applying them.

faq.question: Does it enforce protected branches?
faq.answer: No. It lists recommended branch protections. Repository administrators must configure them.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is plain Markdown and works as context for those coding agents.
